sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
Solitaire Grande's core gameplay revolves around clearing the tableau by creating sequences and suit stacks. The game starts with a standard draw of 1 or 3 cards, and players can draw additional cards from the draw pile or move cards from the freeCells to the tableau. The game has several key elements, including the tableau, freeCells, draw pile, and stockpile. The tableau is where the player's cards are arranged, and the goal is to clear it by creating sequences and suit stacks.

The freeCells are a crucial part of the game, as they provide a safe space for players to move cards around and create sequences. The draw pile is where the player draws new cards from, and the stockpile contains the remaining cards from the draw pile. Players can use the cards in the freeCells to create sequences and suit stacks, which can be moved to the tableau or the foundation piles.

The game also has several special moves, including the ability to move multiple cards at once and the option to undo moves. This feature allows players to experiment with different strategies and learn from their mistakes. With its simple yet engaging gameplay, Solitaire Grande is an excellent choice for players of all ages and skill levels.
